extraction.name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: Xiang Yue et al., MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI, arXiv:2311.16502, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark collection takes three stages. First, common university majors were selected based on the principle that visual inputs are commonly adopted. Second, over 50 university students specializing in these majors were recruited as annotators to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. Annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright regulations and avoid data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. They were also advised to select questions without immediately available answers to prevent data contamination. Finally, data quality control was performed through lexical overlap and source URL similarity checks to remove duplicates, format and typo checking by co-authors, and categorization into difficulty levels, excluding very easy problems.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, and textbooks from six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data quality control involved two steps: identifying potential duplicate problems using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, and distributing problems among co-authors for format and typo checking. Problems were categorized into four difficulty levels, and approximately 10% classified as 'very easy' were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Suspected duplicates were reviewed and eliminated. Co-authors checked for format adherence and corrected deviations. Problems were categorized by difficulty, and those deemed too simplistic were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specialized in the relevant majors served as annotators. They collected questions from textbooks and online resources. The annotation protocol required questions to be accurate, consistent, and adhere to academic rigor. All questions had to contain one or more images, be written in English, meet college-level difficulty, and be unambiguous. Fields annotated included question text, answer options (for multiple-choice), correct answer, image types, question difficulty, and explanation (if available). Questions were stored in JSON format.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Error analysis was conducted on 150 randomly sampled error instances from GPT-4V predictions. Expert annotators identified root causes of mispredictions, categorizing errors into Perceptual (35%), Lack of Knowledge (29%), Reasoning (26%), Textual Understanding (4%), Rejection to Answer (3%), Annotation Error (2%), and Answer Extraction Error (1%).
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in various college majors.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is available at https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/. A live-updating leaderboard is maintained. Version history includes updates to model results, fixes to typos and figure dimensions, and addition of human expert results.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: MMMU aims to stimulate the community to build next-generation multimodal foundation models towards expert artificial general intelligence. It highlights the challenges posed by expert-level tasks and the gap between current models and human experts, indicating significant room for improvement in multimodal understanding and reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI as defined by Morris et al. [57].
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. The benchmark is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI as there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and the '90th percentile of skilled adults'.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) and Large Language Models (LLMs). It is designed to evaluate expert-level multimodal understanding and reasoning across 30 subjects and 183 subfields.
